method: Namur/Roi and Kwajalein are adjudicated separately through night infiltration, US defensive-fire response, and 7-Feb daylight reduction; finite artillery, tank, engineer, CVE and beach-traffic capacity are then recombined. Historical night actions are behavior references only, not result scripts.

US_Dplus1_ground_casualties.note: Includes 6/7-Feb night and 7-Feb daylight ground/landing-area casualties; does not include the separate 5-Feb LST 30-65 personnel effect.

cumulative_main_landing_battles_through_.guard: Do not compare this directly to theater-wide naval/air/LST losses; this is the two main ground assault sectors.

operational_result_T24.Roi: Mopping essentially complete; only tiny isolated hideouts remain.
operational_result_T24.Namur: Organized island defense collapses late afternoon/early evening centered 16:30-19:00. Small isolated groups remain at T24; secure declaration can follow once pockets are checked.
operational_result_T24.Kwajalein: US controls or fire-dominates roughly 65-75 percent of the island, with the stronger axes another 0.8-1.1 km east of the D-Day evening line. Dense northeastern/cantonment strongpoints still retain organized resistance.
operational_result_T24.overall: US victory remains structurally secure. Branch changes raise the D+1 price and preserve more organized Japanese resistance on Kwajalein, but do not recreate a beachhead crisis.

next_frontier: 1944-02-07T24 Marshall local; resolve 7/8-Feb night, Namur final pocket clearance, and Kwajalein D+2 reduction from the surviving northeastern defense.
